title: Annotatio IV §.XIII: Bertram — natural body not corporally present; SIGNUM and SPECIES vs truth; deny oral eating only
pass_a_gloss: (II) About to inculcate that Christ’s natural body is not present in the Supper in a corporal mode, he writes most significantly thus: The Body and Blood which is handled in the Church (i.e. which is treated by the Ministers’ hands in the Church and received by hands and mouth) differs from that body and blood which is known in Christ’s body already glorified through the resurrection: And this Body (namely the Eucharistic bread) is a SIGN and SPECIES; but that is the truth itself. For this is handled until one arrives at that. But when one shall have arrived at that, this will be removed. So it appears they are separated by much difference among themselves — as much as between a pledge and the thing for which the pledge is handed over, and between an image and the thing of which it is the image, and between species and truth. Here let no one think Bertram contends that a shadow and not the truth is taken in the sacrament (for perpetually, as we shall say a little later, he labors to inculcate that the souls of the Faithful are fed in the Sacred Supper with Spiritual food and drink); But what Bertram denies here is this alone: that the true and natural body of Christ is eaten with the Mouth of the body.
pass_b_english: Bertram (II): Christ’s natural body is not present in the Supper in a corporal mode — what ministers handle differs from the glorified body; the Eucharistic bread is SIGN and SPECIES, that is the truth itself (pledge vs thing; image vs reality).
He does not deny truth taken in the sacrament — souls are fed with Spiritual food and drink — he denies only that the true natural body is eaten with the body’s Mouth.
source_text: (II) Naturale corpus Christi, modô corporali, in Cena non præsens esse, inculcaturus, significantissimè ita scribit: Corpus & Sanguis quod in Ecclesia geritur (i. e. quod manibus Ministrorum in Ecclesia tractatur, manibusque & ore accipitur) differt ab illo corpore & sanguine quod in Christi corpore per resurrectionem jam glorificatum cognoscitur: Et hoc Corpus (nempe Eucharisticus panis) SIGNUM est & SPECIES; illud verò ipsa veritas. Hoc enim geritur, donec ad illud perveniatur. Ubi verò ad illud perventum fuerit, hoc removebitur. Apparet ita quod multâ inter se differentia separantur, quantum est inter pignus & eam rem pro qua pignus traditur, & quantum inter imaginem & rem cujus est imago, & quantum inter speciem & veritatem. Hic nemo arbitretur contendere Bertramum, umbram, & non veritatem in sacramento sumi (perpetuò enim, ut paulò post dicemus, cibo Spirituali potuque Fidelium animas in S. Cœna pasci allaborat inculcare); Sed quod negat hic Bertramus, istud solum est: Verum & naturale corpus Christi Ore corporis manducari.

lemmas.gloss: to be eaten with the Mouth of the body

notes: Bertram: SIGNUM/SPECIES; deny oral natural only.
